title: Multitenant status sequencing and prioritization guidelines
author: Nora Kim
content:
Summary:
This document defines how we sequence public and customer-facing status updates for multitenant incidents, how we prioritize customer notifications, and the operational rules SREs and customer success should follow during incidents. It includes an escalation matrix, concrete status page templates, recommended timing windows, and game-day exercises to validate sequencing logic.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted and Dedicated customer incidents that impact more than one customer or have potential cross-tenant impact.
- Not intended for purely internal infra maintenance with zero customer visible impact (see maintenance-runbook).

Key definitions:
- Tenant: an account or customer using Redwood that can be isolated for impacts.
- Degraded: measurable SLO regression (latency/availability) vs baseline.
- Outage: service unavailable or >20% of requests failing for a tenant group for >5 minutes.
- Peripheral impact: non-critical features (metrics, non-blocking logs) are impaired.

Priority tiers (how we prioritize notifying customers):
1) Tier P0 (Broad outage): Multi-region or multi-tenant outage that impacts 30%+ of active requests or core generation API returning 500s. Notify all affected tenants and publish a public status.
2) Tier P1 (Targeted outage high-severity): 1–30% tenant impact or single-tenant but critical customers (SLA contract flagged). Notify impacted tenants individually and publish a public notice if cross-tenant indicators exist.
3) Tier P2 (Degradation): Increased latency or partial feature loss. Notify high-risk tenants (SLA flagged or high traffic) and post a brief public advisory if degradation persists >30 minutes.
4) Tier P3 (Peripheral/low impact): Non-critical features or scheduled work; send private notices only if requested.

Sequencing rules (what gets posted and when):
- Rule 1 — Acknowledge before analysis: Within 10 minutes of detection for Tier P0/P1, publish an acknowledgement on the public status page and open customer-specific tickets for known impacted tenants.
- Rule 2 — Correlate signals: Before composing tenant-specific messages, confirm tenant impact (error logs, routing traces, quota hits). False positives are costly; include evidence in the ticket.
- Rule 3 — Tiered messaging cadence:
  - Tier P0: Acknowledge (T+10m), Update (T+30m), Update every 30m until mitigation, Resolution + RCA within SLO window.
  - Tier P1: Acknowledge (T+15m), Update (T+45m), then hourly.
  - Tier P2: Acknowledge (T+30m) if measurable and customer-facing, updates every 2 hours.
  - Tier P3: As-needed, preference for private communication.
- Rule 4 — Ownership: Status page content must be owned by the Bridge Lead. Customer-specific comms must be coordinated with Customer Success lead before final send for Tier P0/P1.

Escalation matrix (table):
- Columns: Condition | First responder | Bridge lead | CS liaison | Exec notify threshold
- Rows (examples):
  - Multi-tenant outage (>30%): SRE oncall | Senior SRE Bridge Lead | CS Director | Execs at 60 minutes
  - Single critical-customer failure: Product oncall | Eng Manager | Customer Success AE | Execs at 90 minutes if SLA risk
  - Degraded latency (non-blocking): Oncall | Senior SRE | CS Manager (as needed) | Execs if >4 hours and revenue risk

Templates (status page snippets):
- Acknowledgement (public):
  "We are aware of an issue affecting Redwood inference in <region>. Our engineers are investigating. Customers may experience increased latency and intermittent errors. We will post an update within 30 minutes."
- Update (public):
  "Root cause under investigation — current mitigation: routing rollback to stable model variant in progress. Impact: X% of requests in <region>. Next update in 30 minutes."
- Resolution + RCA (public):
  "Service restored at <time>. Root cause: <brief technical summary>. Customer impact: <who/what>. Actions taken: <short list>. RCA and long-term mitigation published in 7 business days."

Customer email/SaaS template (for Tier P1/P0 impacted tenants):
- Subject: "[Action required] Service impact — Redwood inference — <short summary>"
- Body (bulleted):
  - What happened: one-line plain language description.
  - Who was affected: list of impacted tenant IDs or product areas.
  - Current status & mitigation steps: what we are doing now.
  - ETA & next steps: expected cadence and escalation contact.
  - How to reach us: link to customer-specific ticket and CS oncall contact.

Operational checklist (first 30 minutes):
1) Acknowledge on public status page (Bridge Lead).
2) Triage and collect evidence (oncall): request traces, KV cache hit rates, batching backlogs, GPU metrics.
3) Determine tenant impact (tools): run account-impact query, check per-tenant error rates and token-metering anomalies.
4) Open customer tickets and tag SLAs (CS liaison).
5) If rollback or failover is available, prepare plan and estimate blast radius.

Configuration table (recommended thresholds and alerting):
- Alert | Recommended threshold | Pager severity
- 5xx rate (region) | >1% sustained over 3 minutes | P1
- 5xx rate (tenant) | any sustained over 1 minute | P0 for SLA-tagged tenants
- Median p95 latency increase | 2x baseline for 10 minutes | P2
- KV cache eviction spikes | >50% eviction rate in 5m | P1

On-call rotation and handoff notes (implications for sequencing):
- Bridge windows: standard Bridge runs for major incidents should be 2-hour shifts, with explicit handover documents including last status message, outstanding actions, and time-to-next-update.
- Handoffs must include tenant-impact manifest (CSV attachment) so the incoming Bridge Lead can continue customer comms without delay.
- During low-staff windows (nights/weekends), extend acknowledgement windows but maintain the first-update promise (public ack within 20 minutes).

Game-day scenarios (to validate sequencing):
- Scenario A: Regional KV cache hot-eviction causes 503s in one region affecting 12 high-throughput tenants. Objectives: verify tenant-impact query, sequence of public vs private comms, and rollback plan execution. Metrics to validate: mean time to first customer ticket (goal <12m), mean time to public update (goal <15m).
- Scenario B: Silent-entropy model quality regression causes degraded outputs for a small group of enterprise tenants. Objectives: test detection via quality-monitoring alerts, customer-specific messaging and rollback to previous model snapshot, and postmortem quality checks.

Post-incident requirements:
- Evidence capture: attach traces, alert history, tenant-impact CSV, and copies of all customer comms to the postmortem.
- Postmortem timeline: publish an initial timeline within 48 hours; full RCA and action items tracked in the postmortem board within 7 business days.

Decision criteria for public vs private notices (short checklist):
- If more than one tenant is impacted = publish public notice.
- If any SLA-tier customer is impacted = private notice within 30 minutes plus public notice if cross-tenant.
- If impact is internal-only or behind feature flag = private internal notification only.

Ownership and review cadence:
- Document owner: Engineering Reliability (SRE) — contact: sre-docs@redwood.ai (alias).
- Review cadence: quarterly review with CS and Product; after any Tier P0 incident, review within 14 days.

Appendix A: Example customer message (short):
- "We’re investigating increased latency in EU-West affecting generation endpoints. Our team has initiated a routing rollback and will update in 30 minutes. Your account: <tenant-id> shows elevated error rates; we have opened ticket #<id>. For urgent needs contact <CS-oncall>."
